claims.text: Render order: the alarm that means 'somebody built something and never wired it' is first, the good news is last but always present
claims.why: KIND_ORDER starts with INVALID_SNAPSHOT and ends with NOW_REACHED; the comment's stated order matches the tuple

claims.text: NOW_REACHED is good news. TEST_ONLY is a real finding that deliberately does not block
claims.why: NON_BLOCKING_KINDS contains exactly NOW_REACHED and TEST_ONLY, consistent with the claim

claims.text: the acceptance list is wrong, the snapshot contradicts itself and this run looked at less of the tree than the baseline did have to be repaired, not waived
claims.why: ACCEPTABLE_KINDS excludes INVALID_ACCEPTANCE, INVALID_SNAPSHOT, and IGNORE_DRIFT, matching the claim

claims.text: Fenced blocks and generated files are dropped at BUILD time rather than at query time, so there is exactly one place where 'does this text count' is decided
claims.why: build() skips GENERATED_DOCS and fenced lines; sites() only queries the built lines

claims.text: Non-alphanumerics collapse to single spaces before counting, so PKG_TURBO=1 scores 1, not 12
claims.why: _described uses _ALNUM_RUN.sub(' ', rest).strip() and compares to MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS; the example's punctuation and value collapse to a single word

claims.text: The env value is stored VERBATIM rather than hashed: the point is that a reviewer reading the failure can see what was hidden without re-running anything
claims.why: ignore_config stores os.environ.get(IGNORE_ENV,'').strip() directly as 'env'

claims.text: state is what the snapshot stores; sites is runtime-only detail (file:line) used to make remedies actionable, and is deliberately kept OUT of the snapshot
claims.why: This chunk defines the dataclass but does not show where state is serialized or sites is excluded; the claim about snapshot storage is beyond this chunk

claims.text: reach and switches are the reports this state was derived FROM, carried out so no caller has to re-run either engine to ask a follow-up question
claims.why: The dataclass has fields reach and switches, but the claim about derivation and caller convenience is not observable in this chunk

claims.text: git's own floor is 7; a 1-character 'prefix' matches roughly one HEAD in sixteen, and a check that passes by accident is worse than no check because it is believed
claims.why: _MIN_ABBREV is set to 7 and the comment explains the rationale; the value matches the claim

claims.text: The digest proves nobody hand-edited the snapshot. It says NOTHING about when the snapshot was taken -- a baseline generated thirty commits ago verifies its own digest perfectly
claims.why: The digest behavior is in _digest, not in this chunk; the claim about what the digest proves is not verifiable here

claims.text: There is deliberately NO generated_at: a clock reading answers 'when did the generator run', which is the weaker question, and it would destroy the byte-identity this artifact is built on
claims.why: repo_state returns only head, branch, dirty; the absence of generated_at is visible, but the rationale about byte-identity refers to snapshot_bytes, not in this chunk

claims.text: dirty is probed only when there is a .git to probe, so a scan of a tree that is not a checkout costs no subprocess and still answers honestly: None means 'could not tell', never 'clean'
claims.why: repo_state only calls render_mod._dirty when probe_dirty and head != 'unknown'; dirty is set to None when verdict is neither dirty nor clean

claims.text: FAILS CLOSED on the artifact's own defects -- an absent, non-string or malformed repo_state.head means the snapshot cannot say what it scanned
claims.why: snapshot_freshness returns {'fresh': False} when recorded is not a non-empty string

claims.text: FAILS OPEN when the recorded head is well-formed and git cannot answer at all: a tarball checkout with no .git is not evidence of staleness
claims.why: The chunk cuts off at the _SHA_RE.fullmatch check; the fail-open branch is not visible in this chunk

claims.text: Same rule, same reasoning, as daedalus.spine.picker.inventory_freshness
claims.why: The referenced module is not in this chunk; cannot compare

observations.what: snapshot_freshness is cut off mid-function; the rest of its logic (fail-open branch, actual_head comparison) is not in this chunk
DocIndex.build catches OSError on read_text and continues, silently skipping unreadable files; a missing doc file is treated as absent rather than unreadable
repo_state imports render_mod inside the function, not at module top; this is a local import that may hide circular import issues

The comment above KIND_ORDER says 'the alarm that means somebody built something and never wired it is first' but the first entry is INVALID_SNAPSHOT, which is about snapshot corruption, not unwired builds; the comment may refer to a different kind not shown in this chunk
NON_BLOCKING_KINDS and ACCEPTABLE_KINDS are defined but not used in this chunk; their enforcement is elsewhere

risks: DocIndex.build | medium | Unreadable doc files are silently skipped, so a permissions error makes documentation appear absent; a reviewer could believe a switch is undocumented when the file was simply unreadable | Check whether the caller distinguishes missing from unreadable, or whether errors should propagate
todos: Complete snapshot_freshness in next chunk; verify fail-open behavior and actual_head comparison
